final_candidates.decision_summary: Introducing a charged aspartate into the buried hydrophobic core severely destabilizes the fold, promoting subunit knockout.
Replacing the critical buried phenylalanine with aspartate imposes an intolerable energetic and steric penalty on PsaE folding.
Disrupts core packing and buried interactions around the conserved aromatic patch, reliably disrupting the native structure.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidate mutations for folding disruption are well-separated and supported by high confidence.

history.rationale: W17 is a critical buried aromatic residue in the hydrophobic core; introducing an uncompensated negative charge will severely destabilize folding.
W17D is significantly destabilizing according to both sequence PLM and ProteinMPNN, though structurally slightly less penalized than W17P.
Introducing a helix/strand-breaking proline at central core residue W17 disrupts backbone hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic packing.
Proline substitution at Trp17 breaks secondary structure and cavity packing, supported by negative ProteinMPNN ΔlogP -2.44.
Y18 forms essential hydrophobic and packing contacts in the beta-sandwich core; substitution to aspartate introduces a severe desolvation penalty.
Y18D introduces a buried negative charge with a severe structural compatibility penalty (ΔlogP = -3.13), strongly disrupting folding.
I33 is an invariant hydrophobic core residue; mutating it to a charged aspartate disrupts core packing and drives unfolding.
ProteinMPNN strongly favors Asp at position 33 (+1.25 ΔlogP) with moderate PLM tolerance, failing to provide folding disruption.
Proline substitution at core beta-strand position I33 creates steric strain and eliminates the main-chain amide donor, disrupting sheet stability.
ProteinMPNN shows positive conditional compatibility (+0.54), suggesting position 33 readily accommodates Proline without folding collapse.
Position V38 is buried within the central beta-sheet; introducing an aspartate causes electrostatic repulsion and disrupts the hydrophobic interior.
V38D exhibits the lowest structural compatibility (ΔlogP = -5.20) and near-zero sequence plausibility, indicating massive core destabilization.
F40 is a key aromatic residue in the structural core; an aspartate mutation introduces severe electrostatic clashes and prevents proper folding.
Buried hydrophobic Phe replaced by charged Asp strongly destabilizes the hydrophobic core as confirmed by ProteinMPNN ΔlogP -3.51.
Y45 participates in core aromatic packing; replacement with aspartate destabilizes the sheet architecture through charge burial.
ProteinMPNN shows positive compatibility (+0.42), indicating Y45 is likely solvent-accessible and tolerant to Asp.
F48 packs against the hydrophobic beta-barrel interior; substitution with charged aspartate impairs structural stability and folding.
F48D shows strong sequence PLM intolerance but only weak structural incompatibility (ΔlogP -0.22), suggesting partial surface exposure.
L55 is located on a central beta strand; introducing a conformational constraint via proline breaks the strand backbone.
L55P introduces a moderate backbone disruption penalty (ΔlogP -0.45) but displays higher residual sequence plausibility.
